verses.text: When the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, the LORD said to Joshua,
"Choose twelve men from the people, one from each tribe,
and tell them, 'Take twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests stood. Carry them with you and put them down where you camp tonight.'"
So Joshua called the twelve men he had chosen from Israel, one from each tribe.
He said to them, "Go ahead of the box of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan. Each of you lift a stone onto your shoulder, one for each tribe of Israel.
This will be a sign among you. In the future, when your children ask you, 'What do these stones mean?'

tell them, 'The water of the Jordan stopped flowing in front of the LORD's covenant box. When it crossed the Jordan, the water was cut off. These stones will remind the people of Israel of this forever.'"

So the people of Israel did as Joshua told them. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, one for each tribe, as the LORD had told Joshua. They carried them to their camp and put them down there.
Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, where the priests carrying the covenant box had stood. They are still there today.
The priests carrying the box stayed standing in the middle of the Jordan until everything the LORD had told Joshua to do was done, just as Moses had told Joshua. The people hurried across.
When all the people had crossed, the LORD's box and the priests crossed over while the people watched.
The men of Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed, ahead of the people of Israel, as Moses had told them.
About forty thousand men, armed and ready for war, crossed over before the LORD to the plains of Jericho for battle.
That day the LORD made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel. They respected him all his life, just as they had respected Moses.
Then the LORD said to Joshua,
"Tell the priests carrying the box of the covenant law to come up out of the Jordan."
So Joshua told the priests, "Come up out of the Jordan!"
The priests carrying the LORD's covenant box came up out of the river. As soon as their feet touched dry ground, the water of the Jordan flowed back and overflowed its banks as before.
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and camped at Gilgal, on the east side of Jericho.
At Gilgal Joshua set up the twelve stones they had taken out of the Jordan.
He said to the people of Israel, "In the future, when your children ask their parents, 'What do these stones mean?'
tell them, 'Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground.'
For the LORD your God dried up the Jordan in front of you until you had crossed, just as he dried up the Red Sea in front of us until we had crossed.
He did this so that all the peoples of the earth would know that the LORD's power is great, and so that you would always honour the LORD your God."
